title: Credit and Collections Manual: Late Payment Charges on Electric Service Agreement Bills
content:
**Credit & Collections manual: the late payment charge on an Electric Service Agreement bill**

## Section 1: when a bill is charged

A bill that is not paid in full by the end of its grace period is charged once. The charge may be posted only after the bill's due date plus the schedule's late payment grace period has passed without full payment. The grace period is counted in calendar days beginning the day after the due date, and the charge may be posted from the first calendar day after the last grace day. The last grace day itself does not qualify. The dates are read from the company's bill records.

*Hypothetical boundary, for illustration only:* a bill due on 5 June on a schedule with a grace period of 10 days. The grace days run from 6 June through 15 June. On 15 June no charge may be posted; from 16 June, if the bill is still not paid in full, the charge may be posted.

## Section 2: what attracts a charge

- Only one late payment charge is assessed per bill. A bill that already carries a late payment charge is not charged again.
- Late payment charges, fees and program debits never themselves attract a late payment charge.
- The charge is posted only on an agreement in active, notice pending or disconnected status.

## Section 3: bills on which no charge is assessed

- **Income-qualified customers.** No late payment charge is assessed on a residential bill when the customer's income-qualified-until date is on or after that bill's due date.
- **Meter test outstanding.** No late payment charge is assessed on a bill while a customer-requested meter test of the account's meter (a Metering Service record), requested on or before the bill's due date, has no test result recorded yet. Once the result is recorded, the charge may be assessed on the unpaid portion after any accuracy adjustment.

| Hypothetical situation | Late payment charge |
|---|---|
| residential bill due 10 May; income-qualified-until date 10 May | not assessed |
| residential bill due 10 May; income-qualified-until date 9 May | not barred by this exemption |
| meter test requested on the due date, no result yet | not assessed while the result is outstanding |
| meter test requested the day after the due date | not barred by the meter test |

## Section 4: clause no longer in force

The former clause setting the amount of the charge (the schedule's late payment charge rate multiplied by the bill's unpaid portion, rounded to the cent and not less than the schedule's minimum, the unpaid portion being the bill's amount less the payments and credits applied to it by the end of its grace period, with no charge where that portion is zero) is no longer in force and is superseded by the current basis.

superseded_clauses: The charge is the schedule's late payment charge rate times the bill's unpaid portion, rounded to the cent, and not less than the schedule's minimum; the unpaid portion is service_msr_bill_unpaid_portion and no charge arises when it is zero.
